data.narrative:
Orchid is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Noor Siddiqui that has raised $16.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods assessed, only stage-progression analysis was applicable. This method uses the $16.5M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $33M. The peer-median approach could not be executed due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables—while 7 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three qualified at identical or adjacent stages with comparable valuation tiers. Public-comp anchoring, though 3 public-sector peers trade at a 9.2x median price-to-sales multiple, could not be applied because Orchid's revenue is not disclosed.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $28M (low) to $38M (high), centered on $33M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty, particularly given reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy rather than revenue or profitability metrics. Key unknowns include Orchid's revenue trajectory, burn rate, and competitive positioning within the biotech pipeline. A more robust triangulation would require either disclosed financial metrics or access to comparable transaction multiples among the identified private-peer cohort.
